title: Trump Rallies Red States as GOP Battles Michigan Drama and Alaska Legal Defeat
snippet: With just two days before the midterm elections, Republicans face a high-profile Democratic endorsement in Michigan, a federal legal setback in Alaska, and tightening races in traditional conservative strongholds.
content:
With control of Capitol Hill hanging in the balance, President Donald Trump is heading to the Farm Belt to shore up GOP strongholds as Republicans navigate a turbulent final stretch before Tuesday's midterm elections. High-stakes battles in traditionally conservative states, combined with intra-party drama in Michigan and a key courtroom setback in Alaska, have set the stage for an intense election finale.

Intra-Party Rift Shakes Up Michigan Senate Race

In a surprising development, Democratic Representative Haley Stevens publicly endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over her own party's nominee, Abdul El-Sayed. The cross-party endorsement followed a bitter primary battle and a public dispute over campaign messaging, dealing a blow to Democratic unity in a state vital to their hopes of taking control of the U.S. Senate.

Rogers seized on the endorsement to highlight Democratic infighting, while El-Sayed dismissed the move, telling reporters he remains focused on working-class economic issues and reducing the influence of money in politics. Despite the friction, polling suggests El-Sayed maintains a slight edge in the battleground state.

Federal Judge Dismisses Alaska Ballot Challenge

Further north, the Trump administration suffered a legal defeat when a federal judge dismissed a Justice Department lawsuit in Alaska. Federal prosecutors had sought to block election certification over concerns that voters might confuse incumbent Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan with a challenger sharing a similar name, Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.

While Senator Sullivan publicly committed to accepting the election results, GOP Governor Mike Dunleavy signaled he might refuse to certify the race should Democratic Representative Mary Peltola win, adding further uncertainty to the state's post-election landscape.

Trump Heads to Iowa and Kansas Amid Record Early Voting

Trump's final campaign swing takes him to Iowa and Kansas, two reliably red states where Republicans are unexpectedly working to defend Senate seats. Facing slipping approval ratings in rural communities, the administration is making an aggressive push to prevent surprises in the Midwest.

Nationwide turnout has already shattered midterm records, with over 52 million Americans casting early ballots. If Democrats succeed in capturing either chamber of Congress, they will gain significant leverage to challenge Trump's legislative agenda and launch oversight investigations during his final two years in office.
